subject: The lexicon bundle behind the Ukrainian text profiler: top-12000 lemmas with validated CEFR levels, Wiktionary paradigm forms and word families, B1 aspect pairs, and two published lexical minimums, packaged for in-browser lemmatization and coverage profiling
method: lexicon.json: the thread-01 lemma list (rank order) joined per rank to the validated PULS level (null where the profile has none; nothing is guessed), the Wiktionary derivational family id, the aspect-partner pairs from the B1 relation table plus the hand-curated suppletive pairs, and the Borodin A1 and A2 minimums as index sets (with their off-list headwords kept as strings). forms.json: every surface form in the thread-04 Wiktionary paradigm tables mapped to its lemma index, frequency-ordered where a form belongs to several lemmas, omitted where the form equals the lemma. The profiler resolves a token to its exact lemma first, otherwise to the most frequent lemma listed for the form.

files.about: lemmas [lemma, pos, level|null, familyId|null] in rank order; families {id: [lemma indices]}; aspectPairs [[i, j]]; sets {borodinA1, borodinA2: {idx, offList}}; listVersion (the list the indices are ranks on); migrate {from, toIndex} (the previous list's index of every row mapped to its index here, -1 where the row was dropped)
forms {surface form: lemma index | [lemma indices, most frequent first]}
the level-asserted validation texts (learn-ukrainian, CC BY-SA 4.0, attributed) the frozen validation run was computed on: id, level, title, url, text

citation: Lawrence, J. (2026). Ukrainian Frequency: a text profiler for Ukrainian, lexicon bundle (v1.3.0). jakelawrence.xyz/research/ukrainian-frequency/profiler. Lemmas from UberText 2.0 (Chaplynskyi, 2023); paradigm forms and word families from Wiktionary via kaikki.org (CC BY-SA); validated levels from the Ukrainian Vocabulary Profile (Synchak et al., 2025; PULS, by permission, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0); lexical minimums from Borodin et al. (CC BY).
